items.headline: World court finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya
items.summary: It is the first time the International Court of Justice has ruled that a state committed genocide. Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh watched the ruling live.

items.headline: Trump, Putin and Xi hold three-way talks at APEC
items.summary: The US, Russian and Chinese leaders met in Shenzhen; Trump had said he planned to raise nuclear non-proliferation.

items.headline: Denmark approves security deal with Greenland and the US
items.summary: All 109 Danish MPs present backed the agreement, easing tensions over Trump's wish to take over the Arctic island.

items.headline: FTSE 100 falls to six-week low
items.summary: The index dropped 0.93% to 10,452.68 on Thursday, dragged down by defensive heavyweights such as Unilever, National Grid and AstraZeneca.
items.source: BBN Times and Reuters via Euronext, 19 Nov

items.headline: Investec and JD Sports lead London fallers
items.summary: Investec fell about 7.4% and JD Sports about 4.9% after disappointing updates, while Babcock posted strong results.
items.source: Trading Economics and Share Talk, 19 Nov

items.headline: UK consumer confidence weakens as inflation worries grow
items.summary: Gloomier shoppers and concern about energy-driven price rises weighed on London shares, which lagged other European markets.

items.headline: Anthropic shares jump 17% in record stock market debut
items.summary: Priced at $83, the shares opened at $111.50 and closed at $97.17, valuing the Claude maker at about $1.76 trillion. It is the largest IPO ever.

items.headline: US approved nearly 900,000 AI chip sales to China
items.summary: The approvals were granted over six months, Al Jazeera reports, even as Washington tightens other chip controls.

items.headline: Anthropic's debut fails to lift wider AI shares
items.summary: The shares slipped about 4.7% after hours, and OpenAI backer SoftBank slumped as Tokyo stocks fell sharply.
